chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I was sitting at the left of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), and Zurara was at his right. Abu Baseer entered and said, 'O Abu Abdullah, what do you say about the one who doubts in Allah?' He said, 'A kafir (disbeliever), O Abu Muhammad.' He said, 'And (what about) the one who doubts in the Messenger of Allah?' He said, 'A kafir.' Then he turned to Zurara and said, 'He only disbelieves when he rejects (denies with conviction).'

key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurara ibn A'yan, a prominent companion of the Imams

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between doubt and denial in Islamic theology according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the general ruling on doubt (*shakk*) and the specific condition for apostasy (*kufr*) based on the companion Zurara's query. While doubt in Allah or the Prophet is broadly categorized as disbelief, the Imam clarifies to Zurara that true, definitive disbelief (*jahd*) requires conscious denial or rejection of the truth, highlighting the Shia scholarly nuance between mere uncertainty and firm rejection. This hadith is foundational in Usuli jurisprudence for determining the status of the *mushtrak* (one who doubts) versus the *jahid* (one who denies).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Khalaf Bin Hammad, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullahasws, seated on hisasws left, and Zurara was on hisasws right, and Abu Baseer came over and he said, ‘O Abu Abdullahasws! What are youasws saying regarding the one who doubts in Allahazwj’. So heasws said: ‘A Kafir (Unbeliver), O Abu Muhammad!’ He said, ‘So (what about) the doubt in Rasool-Allahsaww?’ So heasws said: ‘A Kafir (Unbeliver)’. Then heasws turned towards Zurara and heasws said: ‘But rather, he disblieves when he rejects’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from Khalaf ibn Hammad from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) sitting to his left side and Zurara was sitting to his right side. Abu Basil’ came in and he asked, ‘What do you say if one doubts in Allah?’ The Imam said, ‘He is an unbeliever, O abu Muhammad.’ Abu Basir then asked, ‘What if one has doubts in the Messenger of Allah?’ The Imam said, ‘He is an unbeliever.’ The narrator has said that the Imam then turned to Zurara and said, ‘He (such a person) is an unbeliever only if he rejects.’”
